questions.question: Distinguish between the UPSC and State Public Service Commissions. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions
  • (SPSCs) are constitutional bodies responsible for recruiting personnel to public services in
  • India. They differ in their jurisdiction, functions and scope of recruitment. UPSC-Established
  • under Article 315 of the Constitution.Functions at the Union level.Recruits candidates for All
  • India Services and Central Government services, as applicable.The President of India
  • appoints the Chairman and members.The President has the authority to remove members
  • under constitutional provisions.Submits its annual report to the President.State Public Service
  • Commission (SPSC)-Established under Article 315 of the Constitution for each
  • state.Functions at the state level. Recruits candidates for state government services.The
  • Governor of the state appoints the Chairman and members.The Governor cannot
  • independently remove members; removal is made by the President under constitutional
  • provisions.Submits its annual report to the Governor.

questions.question: Trace the evolution of administrative reforms in India since independence. Discuss the major committees, commissions and reforms introduced to improve the effectiveness of Indian administration. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Administrative reforms aim to improve efficiency, transparency, accountability and
  • responsiveness in public administration- Since independence, India has introduced several
  • committees, commissions and institutional reforms to modernise administration- Major
  • Committees and Commissions- A.D. Gorwala Report (1951- Paul H. Appleby Reports (1953
  • and 1956]- First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966–1970]- Kothari Committee
  • (1974–1976]- Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2005–2009)- Major
  • Administrative Reforms Introduced- Civil Service Reforms-Panchayati Raj Reforms (73rd
  • Constitutional Amendment, 1992- Urban Local Government Reforms (74th Constitutional
  • Amendment, 1992- Right to Information Act, 2005- E-Governance Initiatives - Citizen's
  • Charters- Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013- Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT]- Mission
  • Karmayogi (2020)- Administrative reforms in India have evolved from improving
  • bureaucratic efficiency to promoting transparent, accountable, decentralised and citizen-
  • centric governance- Effective implementation of reform recommendations remains essential
  • for responsive and good governance.
